summary: ```# Introduction of New Features in Marvelous Designer 12.2 ## Overview of FBX File Format The FBX file format allows you to add or remove multiple virtual models simultaneously. This functionality enables you to integrate other objects or virtual models while keeping the current scene intact. ## Importing FBX Files To import FBX files, follow these steps: 1. Navigate to the menu: **File > Add or Add**. 2. Select the FBX format. 3. Choose the file you need to import and click **Open**. In the FBX dialogue box, ensure you change the load type to **Add**. You can choose either **Avatar** or **Trim** as the target type. ## Import Settings When importing or adding FBX files, they will inherit the same settings as importing OPJ files. Select a copy, then click on the **water glue tool** located at the top right of the location ball, and stick it onto the costume. Repeat the import process to add multiple FBX files and continue with other operations. ## Benefits of Using FBX Format Utilizing the FBX file format to import or remove multiple virtual models enhances your ability to complete multi-role scene production, rather than relying on the content of a single role. ## Target Type Configuration When selecting the FBX file for import: 1. Set the load type to **Add**. 2. Set the target type to **Virtual Model**. For human-type virtual models, click on **Automated Automated Portrait**, which will automatically create a portrait during the import process. ## Object Bar and Animation In the object bar, you can choose the relevant content of the import file, including joint animation. Adjust the axis rotation or input the moving value to position the virtual model correctly. For example, set the moving value on the two-meter Z-axis. If an object is placed below the ground, you can click to align it with the ground. They will automatically be positioned above the ground upon import. ## Positioning Costumes To position a costume accurately, click to move it to the starting point of the action. The costume will automatically adjust to the virtual model near the starting point. After confirming the settings, click to import the file. ## Previewing Animation Open the animation editor to preview the animation. You can import the costume corresponding to the second virtual model, applying the same moving value to ensure they match. ## Simulation and Recording Open the simulation, wear the costume, and begin recording the animation. ## Exporting FBX Files When exporting FBX files, you have the option to export all virtual models or select an independent virtual model for export. ```
